summary: The PR only fixes `__lt__` (`<`) to skip `None` values, but the issue reports that `>`, `<=`, and `>=` crash the same way. My snippet confirms `<` now works while `>`, `<=`, and `>=` still raise `TypeError` on `None` fields. The fix must be applied consistently to all four comparison operators.

checks.evidence: python -m pytest -q -> exit 0, all tests pass
python -c snippet: < OK [1]; > CRASH TypeError; <= CRASH TypeError; >= CRASH TypeError

findings.text: __le__ still uses `lambda value: value <= rhs` without a None guard, crashing on None fields.
__gt__ still uses `lambda value: value > rhs` without a None guard, crashing on None fields.
__ge__ still uses `lambda value: value >= rhs` without a None guard, crashing on None fields.
